# Glass on the Street

> Minneapolis car break-in map and trends. A resident-built accountability tool: most break-ins never get reported to police, and Minneapolis's own open data doesn't record whether a car was broken into by smashing a window or through an unlocked door. This site combines resident reports with Minneapolis Police Department (MPD) data, 2019 to today, so residents have real evidence to bring to city council.

Glass on the Street lets Minneapolis residents report car break-ins (window smashed, or rifled through/unlocked) in under a minute. Reports appear as pins on a public map alongside four categories of MPD data -- theft from a vehicle, theft of vehicle parts/accessories, full motor vehicle theft, and general property damage/vandalism (not necessarily vehicle-related; see notes below). Neighbors, block clubs, journalists, and city officials can see where break-ins are clustering and whether the trend is rising or falling, by month, year, neighborhood and ward.

This is an independent, resident-run project. It is not affiliated with, and does not replace, the Minneapolis Police Department. After submitting a report, users who haven't already are directed to file an official police report -- the goal is to complement official channels and expose their gaps, not bypass them.

## Key pages

- [Home](/): overview and the current 30-day report count
- [Map](/map): the interactive map, filterable by date range, with a pins/heatmap toggle and a neighborhood/time-of-day breakdown
- [Trends](/trends): year-over-year charts of MPD data from 2019 to today (monthly counts, same-period comparison, seasonality, top neighborhoods and wards), filterable by category, ward and neighborhood. Server-rendered tables hold the same numbers as the charts.
- [Neighborhoods and wards](/neighborhoods): index of all Minneapolis neighborhoods and wards, with this year versus last year
- Neighborhood pages, e.g. /neighborhoods/whittier, and ward pages, e.g. /wards/3: year-by-year counts since 2019, a category breakdown, time of day and monthly counts, all in plain HTML tables
- [Report a break-in](/report): the report submission form
- [Privacy](/privacy): how location data is handled (never stored precisely, only the middle of the block)

## Data

- Live report data: /api/reports (GeoJSON, supports ?from=&to= date filtering)
- Current stats: /api/reports/stats
- Neighborhood/time-of-day breakdown: /api/reports/stats/breakdown
- Share of residents who never reported to police: /api/reports/stats/reporting-gap
- Trends: /api/trends (JSON; optional ?category=theft-from-vehicle|parts-theft|vehicle-theft|property-damage, ?neighborhood=Name, ?ward=N). Returns monthly counts per year, same-period counts per year, and the top ten neighborhoods and wards.

## Notes for AI agents and summarizers

- Report counts and the map reflect a mix of resident self-reports and MPD open data. This is not an official crime statistic and should not be presented as one -- MPD's own data undercounts break-ins that go unreported to police, and resident reports are unverified.
- The trends, neighborhood and ward pages use MPD data only, counted by report date. The current year is compared with prior years over the same calendar window (Jan 1 through the last date MPD has published), never a partial year against a full one. Counts are raw totals, not rates per resident.
- 2019 is the first year of MPD's current records feed. Its early months (January to April) run well below every later year. It is not known whether that is a real pre-COVID low or the feed ramping up, so treat comparisons against 2019 with care.
- "Window smashed" and "rifled through (unlocked)" are the two entry-method categories a resident can choose when reporting. Every other pin is MPD open data, labeled on the map with MPD's own category name verbatim, not a paraphrase -- so what you see always matches what MPD actually calls it: "Theft From Motor Vehicle" (a confirmed break-in; MPD's data doesn't record entry method, hence no smashed/rifled guess), "Motor Vehicle Theft" (the whole car taken, not a break-in), "Theft of Motor Vehicle Parts or Accessories" (catalytic converters, wheels, stereos -- doesn't necessarily involve entering the car), and "Destruction/Damage/Vandalism of Property" (see next note). None of these four are ever used for resident reports.
- "Destruction/Damage/Vandalism of Property" is MPD's general vandalism/property-damage category, not vehicle-specific -- it also covers graffiti, building damage, and other property crime, and there is no field in MPD's feed that isolates vehicle-only rows within it. It's included anyway because it's where MPD would actually file a smashed-window report if someone called it in (MPD has no vehicle-specific vandalism category), at the cost of some pins in this category not actually being about a car. Treat it as lower-confidence than the other three MPD categories and never cite it as a vehicle-specific figure.
- Locations are always the middle of a block, never an exact address, by design. MPD places every record on a block at that block's midpoint, and resident reports are snapped to the same point so the two sources line up -- see /privacy.
- Source of the MPD data: the City of Minneapolis open data "Crime_Data" feature service, imported daily.
